description: Changes one or more settings of an existing site; anything left out stays as it is. Takes effect on every edge within about a minute, without publishing again. Settings the plan does not include are refused with the reason. Only change what the person asked for — never invent a password or a date.

comments.description: Who may comment on the site's pages: `off`; `invited` — the people invited with the comment role, on an invite-only site; or `anyone` signed in. Only on plans that include comments.

confirm.description: Required only with `expiryAction: delete`: the site's subdomain, repeated exactly as the person said it. Ask for it rather than filling it in.

expiresAt.description: When the site should come down, as an ISO 8601 instant in the future such as 2026-12-01T09:00:00Z. An empty string cancels a scheduled takedown.

expiryAction.description: What the takedown does, read only with `expiresAt`: `pause` (the default) keeps the files and can be resumed; `delete` removes the site and frees its subdomain, and needs `confirm`.

folder.description: Folder to move the site to — a path such as Clients/Acme or an id from list_folders — or `root` for the top level. Never creates a folder.

forms.description: Whether the site's forms (marked data-drop2run) accept submissions.

invitedOnly.description: True: only the people on the site's list (invite_people) can open it, each signed in. It replaces a password. False: anybody with the link can open it again. Change it only when the person asked who should see the site.

mode.description: How the site serves: `static` answers 404 for a missing path, `spa` falls back to index.html for a client-side router, `docs` reads documents through the viewer. Setting it stops the mode being detected on each publish.

name.description: What to call the site in the dashboard. An empty string clears it.

password.description: A password visitors must type before seeing the site, as the person gave it. An empty string removes the password. On an invite-only site a password replaces invite-only and shuts out everyone on its list, so check get_site's `invitedOnly` and ask first.

site.description: Subdomain or site id, from list_sites.

upstream.description: Sends the site's /api/* calls to an API of the person's own without putting a key in the page. A route is a line in the site's _redirects ending in 200, pointing at this origin — `/api/* https://api.example.com/v1/:splat 200` — published like any other file. Headers the page sends are filtered to a short list, so anything the provider always needs goes in `headers` here. Anybody who can open a public site can call these routes: suggest a key with the least access, and a password or invite-only for an internal tool. Plans without the proxy refuse it.

headers.description: Headers to attach to every call, such as `authorization: Bearer …` or a fixed `anthropic-version`. A value is encrypted on arrival and can never be read back — only its last four characters are shown — so take it from the person, never invent one. A name given again replaces that header.

methods.description: Methods visitors may send; GET only when a new upstream leaves this out. A method that writes lets anybody who opens the site write with the key — add one only when the person asked, and say so.

origin.description: `https://` and a host name, nothing after it, such as https://api.openai.com.

remove.description: True removes the upstream with all its keys; its routes then answer 502.

removeHeaders.description: Header names to drop from this upstream.

name: update_site

comments.description: Who may comment on its pages: nobody, the people invited to comment (only while it is invite-only), or anybody signed in. Null when that could not be read.

expiresAt.description: When it is scheduled to come down, or null.

expiryAction.description: What the takedown does: `pause` or `delete`, or null when none is scheduled.

folderId.description: The folder it is filed in, or null at the top level.

invitedOnly.description: Whether only invited people can open it, or null when that could not be read. Null does not mean public.

name.description: What it is called, or null.

passwordProtected.description: Whether visitors must type a password.

title: Change a site's settings
